title: Change of finite coefficients for compact support
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism in the finite-field datum.
Put $A=A_{E,n}$, $B=A_{E,m}$, where $1\leq m\leq n$.
For a bounded constructible complex $K$ of
finite Tor amplitude, the
canonical coefficient comparison is an isomorphism

$$
(Rf_!K)\otimes_A^L B\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\
Rf_!(K\otimes_A^L B).
$$

Here the right side uses $B$-coefficients and
compact support; the map
comes from the tensor
comparison. It is compatible with successive reductions, pullback,
and the counits defining the projection transformation.

proof.text: Write $S_T^{A,B}=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T:D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ and $U_T^{A,B}$ for scalar restriction. These are different coefficient categories. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $S_T^{A,B}$ is computed by $P\otimes_A B$ for a K-flat resolution $P$ with flat terms, which exists by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-change-of-rings-tensor-comparison], forgetting this representative is the same total tensor complex that computes $M\otimes_A^L B_T$ in $D(A_T)$. The canonical derived adjunction at the identity ringed-topos map $h_T:(T,B_T)\to(T,A_T)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] gives $S_T^{A,B}\dashv U_T^{A,B}$. Scalar restriction is exact and reflects isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. For a scheme map $u:T\to V$, the identified constant-coefficient inverse images give a canonical comparison $\lambda_u:u_B^{-1}S_V^{A,B}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_T^{A,B}u_A^{-1}$. On a K-flat representative it sends the inverse image of $x\otimes b$ to $u^{-1}x\otimes b$. Pullback preserves these K-flat models by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Thus this is a comparison in the B-module category and is compatible with coefficient multiplication, not just an underlying-A identification.

Choose the compactification $c=(j,p)$ used in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], so $Rf_!^A=Rp_*^A j_!^A$. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], choose $K_e\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $
u_X^*K_e\cong K$. Extension by zero is exact and left adjoint to restriction by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]; etale extension by zero is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. Its comparison with the etale functor is [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], extended termwise to complexes. In particular $E=j_!^A K$ is the bounded etale-origin object $
u_{ ar X}^*E_e$, $E_e=j_!^{\mathrm{et}}K_e$. If K has Tor interval $[a,b]$, its tensor with the degree-zero sheaf $B_X$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$, directly by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The open tensor isomorphism [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula] gives $E\otimes_A^L B_{ ar X}\cong j_!^A(K\otimes_A^L B_X)$, so this object too is bounded. By the monoidal comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], it equals $
u_{ ar X}^*(E_e\otimes_A^L B_{ ar X,\mathrm{et}})$. The exact comparison on sheaves has an isomorphic unit by [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level], hence reflects zero sheaves. It follows that $E_e\otimes_A^L B_{ ar X,\mathrm{et}}$ is bounded as well. These checks supply the bounded-below inputs needed for the site comparisons below; no assertion that B is perfect over A is used. The same K-flat calculation, with the comparison morphism $
u_T$ in place of a scheme morphism, gives an isomorphism $
u_{T,B}^*(K_e\otimes_A^L B)\cong S_T^{A,B}(
u_{T,A}^*K_e)$ in D(B). The comparison is exact and reflects zero cohomology sheaves also for the finite ring B. Thus $K_e\otimes_A^L B$ is bounded, and this displayed B-linear isomorphism supplies an etale-origin witness for $S_X^{A,B}K$, not merely for its restriction to A. Applying the exact open functors supplies the witness for $j_!^B S_X^{A,B}K$ as well.

proof.text:
For every scheme map $u:T\to V$ define the B-linear comparison $\chi_{u,M}:S_V^{A,B}Ru_*^A M\to Ru_*^B S_T^{A,B}M$ to be the mate of $\lambda_u$ under the canonical derived adjunctions. Explicitly its transpose is
$$u_B^{-1}S_V^{A,B}Ru_*^A M\xrightarrow{\lambda_u}S_T^{A,B}u_A^{-1}Ru_*^A M\xrightarrow{S_T^{A,B}\varepsilon^A_{u,M}}S_T^{A,B}M.$$
This is exactly the mate construction of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Under the canonical scalar-restriction/direct-image identification of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], its restriction is the A-linear projection arrow $\pi_{u,M,B_V}:Ru_*^AM\otimes_A^LB_V\to Ru_*^A(M\otimes_A^LB_T)$. Indeed, transpose after scalar restriction using that node's adjunct formula: the transpose is $(\varepsilon^A_{u,M}\otimes1)t_u$, precisely the definition in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. The comparison of step 1 identifies the tensor representatives, so the two transposes, and hence their adjuncts in D(A), coincide. This identifies the underlying map of an already constructed B-arrow; it does not try to lift an arbitrary A-arrow to D(B).

The proper map p is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, as required by the comparison theorem. In fact proper includes finite type and a closed diagonal by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; finite type includes quasi-compactness by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], the preimage of any affine under its diagonal is an affine spectrum of a quotient ring, which is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Thus the diagonal is quasi-compact, which is quasi-separatedness by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism].

proof.text: Apply [lem-etale-proper-projection-formula-finite] to p, the finite commutative ring A, $M=E_e$, and $N=B_{Y,\mathrm{et}}$. It makes the actual etale projection arrow an isomorphism; that theorem allows arbitrary unbounded N and does not require N to be perfect. The comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] applies to both $E_e$ and $E_e\otimes_A^L B_{\bar X,\mathrm{et}}$ by steps 2 and 4, and says that the named direct-image comparison is an invertible counit mate. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the ringed square with vertical maps $p_{\mathrm{et}},p_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and horizontal maps $\nu_Y,\nu_{\bar X}$, taking $Q=B_{Y,\mathrm{et}}$. Together with the canonical monoidal comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], its equality identifies the pullback of that etale projection arrow with $\pi_{p,E,B_Y}$, through these two invertible direct-image comparisons. Thus $\pi_{p,E,B_Y}$ is an isomorphism on the pro-etale site. Step 3 identifies it with the restriction of $\chi_{p,E}$, and [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] reflects isomorphisms, so $\chi_{p,E}$ is an isomorphism in D(B). No conservativity assertion for geometric stalks of arbitrary pro-etale complexes is needed.

proof.text:
There is a canonical B-linear isomorphism $\beta_j:S_{\bar X}^{A,B}j_!^A\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!^B S_X^{A,B}$. To fix its normalization, use the two adjunctions $S\dashv U$ of step 1 and $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. The right adjoints of the two displayed left adjoints are respectively $j_A^{-1}U_{\bar X}^{A,B}$ and $U_X^{A,B}j_B^{-1}$, identified by restriction of the same underlying module sheaf. Transposing this identity defines beta; the inverse is obtained by transposing the inverse identity, and the triangle identities show their products are identities. For an explicit normalization put $\delta_j=\beta_j^{-1}:j_!^B S_X^{A,B}\to S_{\bar X}^{A,B}j_!^A$. Its transpose under $j_!^B\dashv j_B^{-1}$ is
$$S_X^{A,B}K\xrightarrow{S_X^{A,B}(\eta^A_{j,K})}S_X^{A,B}j_A^{-1}j_!^AK\xrightarrow{\lambda_{j,j_!^AK}^{-1}}j_B^{-1}S_{\bar X}^{A,B}j_!^AK.$$
After restriction to A this is the unit tensored with B. It is consequently the transpose of the inverse of the open tensor comparison of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula]. Hence the restriction of beta, in the displayed forward direction, is that open tensor comparison. Form
$$\chi_f^c(K)=(Rp_*^B\beta_{j,K})\circ\chi_{p,j_!^AK}:S_Y^{A,B}Rf_!^AK\longrightarrow Rf_!^BS_X^{A,B}K.$$
Both factors are isomorphisms. After restriction of scalars, identify its target by [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. Step 3 and the normalization of beta identify this arrow with the compactified tensor comparison of [def-exchange-projection], in the compactification fixed by [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Hence it is the stated coefficient comparison, with its actual B-module structure.

For a further quotient $B\to C=A_{E,r}$, $1\le r\le m$, use a K-flat A-model P for each input. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], $P\otimes_A B$ is K-flat over B, so successive scalar extension is computed by $(P\otimes_A B)\otimes_B C\cong P\otimes_A C$. The identification sends $(x\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $x\otimes\bar b c$ and is associative for a third quotient. The comparisons lambda of step 1 agree under it. Apply the pasting-along-G,H formula of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] with $G=S_V^{A,B}$ and then $S_V^{B,C}$ and corresponding H on the source site. The mate of the composite lambda is consequently
$$\chi_u^{A,C}=\chi_u^{B,C}\circ S_V^{B,C}(\chi_u^{A,B}),$$
with the first factor evaluated at $S_T^{A,B}M$ and the canonical scalar-associativity identifications understood. For beta_j the same assertion follows by transposing the composite identity $j^{-1}U^{A,B}U^{B,C}=U^{A,B}U^{B,C}j^{-1}$; uniqueness of adjoints makes this the beta for A to C. Substituting these two equations in the formula of step 6 proves the successive-reduction identity for chi_f, including the identity for m=n. The restriction comparisons used at the endpoints are transitive by [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. These are identities in D(C), not conclusions inferred from faithfulness of derived scalar restriction.

proof.text:
For a cartesian base-change square $(f,f',g,g')$, with arbitrary $g$ between schemes in the datum, compute compact support using c and its base change. The proper/open formula is [def-cbc-exchange-map], and [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] specifies its transported pro-etale exchange. On the proper factors, coefficient exchange chi_p and geometric exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_p$ are mates of, respectively, the square $p_B^{-1}S_Y\cong S_{\bar X}p_A^{-1}$ and the inverse-image commutation square for $(p,p',g,\bar g')$. The two pastings of these squares are the same B-linear inverse-image comparison: on K-flat models both apply the commuting inverse images to x and attach the coefficient b, $x\otimes b\mapsto(\bar g')^{-1}p^{-1}x\otimes b$. The two pasting formulas of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] therefore equate their mates.

For the open square write $e_j^D:\bar g_D'^{-1}j_!^D\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!'^D g_D'^{-1}$, for $D=A,B$, using the actual pro-etale isomorphism of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. Its inverse, rather than e itself, is the adjunction mate under $j_!'^D\dashv j_D'^{-1}$ of
$$g_D'^{-1}K\xrightarrow{g_D'^{-1}(\eta^D_{j,K})}g_D'^{-1}j_D^{-1}j_!^DK\cong j_D'^{-1}\bar g_D'^{-1}j_!^DK.$$
The corresponding etale base-change map is the isomorphism of [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change]. Compare the two routes obtained by pasting this square with beta_j and beta_j' of step 6. Invert e and beta and transpose under the open adjunctions. Using the displayed formula and the formula for delta in step 6, both routes apply scalar extension to $g_A'^{-1}(\eta^A_{j,K})$ and then use lambda to identify its target with $j_B'^{-1}S_{\bar X'}\bar g_A'^{-1}j_!^AK$. Indeed the coefficient tensor sends $x\otimes b$ to $g'^{-1}(\eta^A_{j,K})(x)\otimes b$ on both routes; the inverse-image and coefficient comparisons act identically on x and b. The transposes coincide in D(B), so the open squares commute. The construction is degreewise on sheaves, hence remains the same for the etale-origin realizations and their site comparisons.

Composing the proper and open equalities gives
$$\operatorname{Ex}_!^B\,g^{-1}(\chi_f^{A,B})=\chi_{f'}^{A,B}\,S_{Y'}^{A,B}(\operatorname{Ex}_!^A),$$
after $g^{-1}S_Y\cong S_{Y'}g^{-1}$ and its source-site analogue. The site comparisons in steps 2 and 5 identify this composite with the transported one: pasting its proper square with the comparison morphisms gives the counit transpose of step 5, and pasting its open square gives the displayed unit transpose. The mate-pasting bijections identify the corresponding arrows, including their directions. Thus the exchange is the specified proper/open composite of [def-cbc-exchange-map]; [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] supplies its isomorphism property on the bounded-below etale-origin inputs checked in step 2. Thus the equality compares the geometric exchange in each coefficient category. The theorem is not being used as a coefficient-change or open-adjunction normalization statement.

proof.text:
Finally, the defining transpose of chi_p in step 3 gives the counit equation
$$\varepsilon^B_{p,S_{\bar X}M}\circ p_B^{-1}(\chi_{p,M})=S_{\bar X}(\varepsilon^A_{p,M})\circ\lambda_{p,Rp_*^AM}.$$
For arbitrary $Q\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, as allowed by the current finite-level ambient definition [def-exchange-projection], apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the square whose vertical maps are $p_A,p_B$ and whose horizontal maps are the coefficient ringed-topos maps $h_Y,h_{\bar X}$ of step 1. Inserting its canonical tensor identifications gives the equality in D(B)
$$\chi_{p,M\otimes_A^Lp_A^{-1}Q}\circ S_Y(\pi^A_{p,M,Q})=\pi^B_{p,S_{\bar X}M,S_YQ}\circ(\chi_{p,M}\otimes_B^L1).$$
This is precisely coefficient compatibility of the proper projection transformation, and identifies its defining counit rather than merely its endpoints. For the open piece, beta_j is normalized by the identity of right adjoints. Its transpose carries the unit of $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ to that same unit after S, and tensoring this unit with Q gives the open projection comparison on either route; the equality is just $(x\otimes q)\otimes b\mapsto(x\otimes b)\otimes(q\otimes1)$ with the balanced tensor identifications, computed on the K-flat models of step 1. Composing the proper equation with this open equation and using the definition of the compactified projection transformation in [def-exchange-projection] proves the asserted compatibility for compact support. Thus every compatibility is established for the B-linear arrow constructed in step 6; no flatness of A to B, finite projective resolution of B, or faithfulness of the derived restriction functor has been assumed.
